reasoning: Combined both proposals into one replacement of the existing exact-answer-granularity rule. It now covers clue-matched lexical form, canonical terminology and number, concise category handling, and preserving context-supported honorifics without adding unnecessary titles. Both source patches support this consolidated rule.

edits.target: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, using the concise form most directly supported by the clue and its evidence. Do not add an unnecessary corporate suffix or title subtitle, or repeat wording already supplied by the clue. For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than substituting a familiar nickname when the full name is the relevant answer. When a category is already specified, provide the distinguishing value rather than repeating the category.
edits.content: - Give the shortest unambiguous answer at the requested granularity, in the conventional lexical form and part of speech called for by the clue (for example, an adjective or demonym rather than its associated country). Prefer the exact context-supported term over a close synonym or related term, and preserve its canonical part of speech and number; plural clue wording does not always mean the answer label itself should be plural. When the clue already supplies the category or type, return the distinguishing value alone: do not append a generic category noun, institution label, explanatory wording, or unnecessary title, subtitle, or suffix unless needed for disambiguation. For a person, use an explicitly supported full personal name rather than a familiar nickname when the full name is relevant, and preserve honorifics that are part of the context-supported conventional name, especially when the clue cues them.
